image:image.image:title: Pairing end to end, in twelve seconds — no account, no cable.
image:image.image:caption: Screen recording of Relay pairing: the PC recognises the phone and its two-digit code, one click connects, and the phone reports one device connected.

image:image.image:title: The phone side: live traffic, a two-digit code, and a QR for the PC to scan.
image:image.image:caption: Relay on Android: one device connected, 4.2 GB up and 3.0 GB down, the two-digit pairing code, and a QR code.

image:image.image:title: The PC side stays out of the way — it lives in the system tray.
image:image.image:caption: Relay on Windows: a compact window offering Scan QR or Enter Code Manually.

image:image.image:title: Today asks for one boulder — not a list you will never finish.
image:image.image:caption: Flow's Today screen in Persian: the day's single boulder with a start-focus button, habits, and free time.

image:image.image:title: One target on screen, and a ring that only counts down.
image:image.image:caption: A focus session running against the day's target, a ring counting down from twenty-five minutes.

image:image.image:title: When focus breaks, Flow captures why instead of losing it.
image:image.image:caption: A sheet asking what broke the session, with chips for tiredness, people, phone, and intrusive thoughts.

image:image.image:title: The Mirror shows the week as it was — including the zero-hour days.
image:image.image:caption: A weekly review: deep-work hours over seven days and a thirty-day pattern of what interrupts most.

image:image.image:title: Purchase price in, profit percentage in, selling price out — in one screen.
image:image.image:caption: Screen recording of Sooda: choosing Persian, typing a purchase price and a profit percentage, and the selling price counting up to the result.

image:image.image:title: Persian numerals throughout, right to left, with the result laid out to be read aloud.
image:image.image:caption: Sooda in Persian on a phone: 850,000 at 35 percent gives a selling price of 1,147,500 and a profit of 297,500.

image:image.image:title: The same app in English — one build, two languages.
image:image.image:caption: The same calculation in English on a phone, showing a selling price of 1,147,500 and a profit of 297,500.

image:image.image:title: Three modes — profit, sell price, discount — behind one set of tabs.
image:image.image:caption: Sooda in a desktop browser in Persian, with tabs for profit percentage, sell price, and discount.

image:image.image:title: Every task carries the one number that matters: how long it takes.
image:image.image:caption: Nava's task list in light mode: a focus ring at two of three, tasks with durations, and a completed section.

image:image.image:title: Dark mode is a real theme, not an inverted screenshot.
image:image.image:caption: The same task list in dark mode, with identical layout and contrast.

image:image.image:title: Start a task and it becomes a timer — the estimate is the session.
image:image.image:caption: A forty-five minute focus timer for a study task, with plus-five and minus-five controls.

image:image.image:title: Adding a task takes one sheet and no navigation.
image:image.image:caption: The new-task sheet: title, tags for personal and twenty-five minutes, pin, reminder, and subtasks.

image:image.image:title: A product preview of the desktop window — disk usage by category, safe to clean.
image:image.image:caption: Purify's product preview: a desktop window showing disk usage broken down by category with a safe-clean action.

image:image.image:title: The menu: three modes, and a code box for joining a friend's room.
image:image.image:caption: The OVERRUN title screen: the wordmark over a dark arena, with three mode cards below it.

image:image.image:title: Wave 14, and the banner says THEY LEARN. The director composes the wave against your build.
image:image.image:caption: Wave 14 of co-op: dozens of enemies converging on a single player in a pale concrete arena.

image:image.image:title: A 10x combo. The ladder starts decaying 3.2 seconds after the last kill.
image:image.image:caption: Two explosions going off at once, damage numbers rising, a ten times combo counter on screen.

image:image.image:title: Wave 20, a boss. Every rose ring is a telegraphed attack — rose is never decorative.
image:image.image:caption: A boss twice the height of everything else, telegraphed slam rings marked in rose across the floor.

image:image.image:title: Team deathmatch, 22–19. Team colour is gameplay information, so it lives in the shared package.
image:image.image:caption: Team deathmatch at 22 to 19, blue and orange players trading fire across a symmetric arena.

image:image.image:title: Squad royale with 29 seconds left. Rose means the floor is being taken away from you.
image:image.image:caption: Squad royale with four scores on the HUD and the arena's rose closing zone eating the left half of the floor.

image:image.image:title: Wave 7, and the arena is briefly empty. The relief valley is deliberate; it is what makes the next spike land.
image:image.image:caption: A quiet moment on wave 7: one player alone on a wide concrete floor, the arena tinted rose on one side.

image:image.image:title: On a phone, landscape and fullscreen. The HUD stays at the edges because the centre is where you are staying alive.
image:image.image:caption: The same game on a phone in landscape, with a floating dash pad and thumb controls at the edges.
